source_title: Civilization #25: Paul of Tarsus, Messiah of Rome
summary: This older Paul lecture is already public as Eschatology evidence for messianic victory recoded as adaptation to Rome, while adding Christian-origin pressure around Christianity as a religion about Jesus, Paul as franchiser/strategist, faith shifting from inner experience to required belief, and priestly interpretation replacing direct access.

new_lens_seeds.title: Messianic Victory Recoded As Imperial Adaptation

new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare Paul's Rome-facing Christianity, later Christian empire formation, Grand Inquisitor obedience, Holy Empire scripts, and modern movements that convert promised rupture into institutional adaptation.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: The mechanism is already represented by the public Eschatology lens point; hold this as seed language rather than creating a new child page.

new_lens_seeds.title: Franchise Religion Replaces Direct Teaching
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A direct spiritual teaching can become scalable by changing the center from what the teacher taught to belief in the teacher as a franchisable object, then using organization, salesmanship, hierarchy, and interpretation to spread.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The seed can compare Paul/Ray Kroc, Catholic tradition, imperial scripture, school canons, platform religion, and any guide system where access to truth becomes a reproducible franchise.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed only. It is too close to Religion As Administrative Filter and Guide Trap to become a standalone public page without broader multi-source comparison.
